newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 - Latest official figures on CPO production and palm oil stocks in October were within estimate released in our previous two reports. CPO production rose 2.2 percent or 18,800 tonnes to 883,600 tonnes. East Malaysia contributed the bulk of the increase when production increased 13,300 tonnes or six percent to 231,600 tonnes. Production in Peninsular Malaysia was marginally higher by 0.8 percent. On an annual basis, production in the country remained strong with a growth of 15 percent.

This exceeded the growth of eight perrcent posted in the 1st nine months of this year. For the remaining 2 months of the year, the pace of growth will slow down to less than the 8.9 percent recorded in the 10 months to October. On a month-on-month basis, production this month is tentatively to drop 13 percent to around 770,000 tonnes. Production in first-half-November fell between 15-20 percent due to fewer working hours arising from the Deepavali holidays on November 10-11. Production this month may also be affected by weather conditions as the rainy season has started this week.

So far widespread showers and/or thunderstorms occured mostly in the late afternoon or evenings. Despite recorded high palm oil exports in October, palm oil stocks rose for the third consecutive month. Stocks at end October rose 58,800 tonnes to 953,200 tonnes, or slightly less than our estimate of 965,000 tonnes. As expected, the buildup in stocks was entirely in the form of CPO and in Peninsular Malaysia. At 601,200 tonnes, CPO stocks were up by 76,800 tonnes with the increase in Peninsular Malaysia alone amounting to 90,600 tonnes.

Almost all refiners were well stocked up. We expect the situation to be extended to this month - possibly to December - as a precaution or hedge against disruptions in delivers due to floods during the rainy season. Palm oil exports reached an all-times recorded high of 727,629 tonnes October according to figures released by PORLA. This compared with 649,688 tonnes in September revised and the previous high of 687,870 set in August. Exports in January-October totalled 5.922 million tonnes, up from 5.468 million tonnes in the same period last year.

Similarly, despite robust PKO exports of 49,379 tonnes in October as against 39,782 tonnes in September, stocks of PKO/PK rose further to 183,200 tonnes from 168,400 tonnes, oil basis, at end September. Stocks of palm oil now appear unlikely to reach the one million tonne level due chiefly to better than expected exports. However, supplies remain ample with end-November stocks tentatively estimated to reach 980,000 tonnes as against some 798,000 tonnes a year earlier. Palm price held firm at the start of this week led by gains in futures which reflected mainly speculative buying.
February futures settled 22 ringgit higher at 1,220 ringgit on Monday before pulling back somewhat to 1,207 ringgit yesterday but still higher than 1,190 ringgit a week earlier (November 13).
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
